title: Byzantine-Resilient Over-the-Air Federated Learning under Zero-Trust Architecture

C-a.quote: adaptive clustering (FedSAC). FedSAC aims to protect a portion of the devices from attacks through zero trust architecture (ZTA) based Byzantine identification and adaptive device clustering.
C-a.locator: Abstract; two stages with a stated protection purpose in that sentence, plus the weighting stage which acts on the identification's output, "devices identified as Byzantine have their weighting factor set to 0, causing their reputations frozen" (§IV). The identification stage's own description is at §I, "Byzantine identification method using historical reputation based on ZTA", and its rule at §IV, "Hence, we identify the M devices with the lowest reputation as the Byzantine devices in the current round". AMENDMENT 3 CAVEAT RECORDED: the clustering stage also carries a communication purpose, and where the paper strips its defense role it describes it as "conducted only for noise minimization" (§V), so the C-a count rests on the abstract's protection sentence and would not survive a reading that took the noise-minimization description as the clustering stage's whole purpose

C-b.quote: quantization compromises performance and majority voting ... is inadequate in withstanding formidable Byzantine attacks.
C-b.locator: §I; the deficiencies the paper names are those of PRIOR clustering-based schemes, offered as motivation for the framework as a whole, not as a reason for pairing its own constituents. The integration of the two stages is stated as a fact and as an optimization convenience rather than as a choice made on constituent properties: "By integrating the sequential clustering into (P2) and using the knowledge about identified Byzantine devices, we rewrite the optimization of the weighting factors" (§IV), and "we introduce a sequential clustering method, transforming the joint optimization into a weighting optimization problem without sacrificing the optimality" (§I). No quotation gives a reason for pairing identification with clustering or with weighting

C-c.quote: learning performance with the MNIST dataset in Fig. 4. FedSAC is seen to outperform the existing baselines across all types of attacks, with a negligible performance gap compared to the ideal case.
C-c.locator: §V; the metric is the assembled scheme's own test accuracy under attack ("Fig. 4. Test accuracy for the MNIST dataset and different types of attacks. (a) Sign-flipping attack (b) Gaussian attack (c) Label-flipping attack"), across SNRs and Byzantine configurations

C-d.quote: Random clustering [27]–[29]: Clustering-based robust aggregation is performed and device clustering is randomly determined. • w/o adaptive weighting: The sequential clustering is conducted only for noise minimization and the weighting ... The last two baselines can be interpreted as ablation experiments of the proposed approach, thus validating the effectiveness of each component in the proposed FedSAC.
C-d.locator: §V; the elision in the quotation skips a displayed fraction that pdftotext extracts out of order -- the w/o-adaptive-weighting arm sets the weighting factors to 1/K, and the extracted stream renders it as "the weighting 1 . factors are set as K", so the span is cut before it rather than silently repaired. The code rests on the RANDOM CLUSTERING arm, which substitutes the upstream clustering rule while the downstream robust aggregation and adaptive weighting are held fixed, and the paper reads the composed outcome off that substitution: "test accuracy when juxtaposed with existing random clustering schemes. FedSAC achieves performance comparable to random clustering in approximately 420 communication rounds, thereby reducing the number of rounds by 47.5%". The w/o-adaptive-weighting arm removes the DOWNSTREAM stage and is the declined direction. A second, analytic route is present at the Abstract and §III: "By conducting a one-step convergence analysis, we theoretically characterize the convergence behavior with different device clustering mechanisms and uneven aggregation weighting factors for each device"

C-e.quote: By repeating this analysis, we conclude that all Byzantine devices are correctly identified in the steady state regardless of the specific type of attack.
C-e.locator: §IV, the mechanism-attribution claim for the identification stage, derived rather than measured; the mechanism condition is stated alongside it, "Accurate Byzantine identification, tailored to different attack strategies, can be achieved by selecting a sufficiently large α, thus preventing the occurrence of error traps", and the empirical constituent-level claim is the 47.5% round reduction attributed to the clustering rule in §V

coder_note:
C-b = NO IS THE DECIDING CODE AND IT IS A CLOSE CALL, RECORDED IN FULL SO A READER CAN OVERTURN IT. This paper has C-a, C-c, C-d and C-e all YES; C-b alone keeps it out of the DESIGN count. The searches that came back empty: the aid's C-b bucket returned 16 candidates, all of them about privacy, the MINLP reformulation or the simulation plan; three targeted greps for a pairing reason (clustering-purpose clauses, reputation-purpose clauses, and however/but adjacent to clustering or weighting) returned only critiques of PRIOR work and statements of how the stages are wired together. The paper's own framing of why it composes is optimization-theoretic -- inserting the clustering into the problem makes a joint optimization tractable as a weighting optimization -- which is a reason of a fifth kind, but it is a reason about MATHEMATICAL CONVENIENCE, not about constituents being individually effective or covering complementary threats, and C-b's frozen text admits only the latter two. Rule 3 also points this way: where a quotation supports two readings, take the one that does not make the paper outcome-gated. Overturning C-b would move this row into DESIGN but NOT into the primary count, because C-d = YES independently.

THE C-d ARM IS A CLEAN UPSTREAM SUBSTITUTION AND THE PAPER LABELS IT AN ABLATION ITSELF. Random clustering replaces FedSAC's sequential/adaptive clustering rule with a random one and changes nothing downstream: the same robust aggregation, the same adaptive weighting, the same attacks, the same SNRs. That is the SPFL shape (substitute the upstream, hold the rest) and it is cleaner than SPFL's, because what varies is a single rule rather than a construction procedure. The paper then reports the outcome difference in rounds-to-target and attributes it to the clustering rule. The companion arm, w/o adaptive weighting, deletes the downstream stage and is the DROPlet direction; the paper presents both as "ablation experiments" in one breath, which is a good illustration for A5 that the word ablation does not distinguish the two directions and that the rubric's distinction has to be applied by reading the arm, not the label.

AMENDMENT 3 IS GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS HERE AND THE ROW DISCLOSES IT RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT SILENTLY. Device clustering in over-the-air FL serves two purposes at once: it forms virtual devices whose analog superposition suppresses channel noise, which is a COMMUNICATION purpose, and it is the substrate of the clustering-based robust aggregation, which is a DEFENSE purpose. The paper says both, in different places -- the abstract attributes protection to "adaptive device clustering", and §V's ablation baseline describes clustering "conducted only for noise minimization" when the defense-side weighting is stripped. Amendment 3 requires purpose to be quoted rather than inferred, and both quotations exist, so I coded C-a = YES on the abstract and recorded the counter-quotation. This is the first row in the frame where a single component has two stated purposes in the same paper, one of which Amendment 3 counts and one of which it excludes. A5 must report it as a limit of the amendment's purpose test: the test resolves a component whose name misleads, and it does not resolve a component that genuinely does two jobs.

DOMAIN NOTE: this is the frame's first over-the-air / analog-aggregation paper, and its inclusion is correct under the frozen screen -- it proposes and evaluates a defense against Byzantine devices in FL. Its presence is useful because the physical-layer setting supplies a non-defense purpose for a defense-shaped component, which is the exact configuration Amendment 3 was written for and, as above, does not fully settle.

TWO QUOTATIONS REPAIRED AFTER CODING, AND ONE EXPOSES AN EXTRACTION HAZARD THE FRAME HAD NOT SEEN. This is an IEEE two-column paper, and pdftotext interleaves the columns, so the sentence "However, low-precision quantization compromises performance and majority voting is inadequate in withstanding formidable Byzantine attacks" arrives split by text from the adjacent column. My C-b quotation had spliced the adjacent column's word "clustering" into it, yielding a sentence the paper does not contain. The C-d quotation had similarly healed a displayed fraction (1/K) that extracts out of order. Both are now explicit multi-span elisions. C-b = NO and C-d = YES are unchanged.
